title: Pilot scope & seller-guided playbook (working draft)
content:
PURPOSE:
This is a compact, seller-facing playbook and pilot-scope template intended for fast technical qualification and a repeatable pilot kickoff. Draft is intentionally concise so sellers can run a 20–30 minute technical handoff with minimal prep.

OVERVIEW / ONE-LINER SELLER PLAY: 
- Run a tight technical qualification, establish a 2-week sandbox pilot with defined success metrics, and secure a follow-on commitment (either Dedicated evaluation or production POC).
- Emphasize predictable latency, cost controls (batching/caching), and fallback model policy up front.

PILOT SUMMARY (SELLER SCRIPT):
- 0–5m: Position Redwood value: production economics, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, and predictable rollouts.
- 5–15m: Technical qualifier + handshake with integrator/infra owner. Cover endpoints, sample QPS, peak concurrency, and PII/data flow.
- 15–20m: Agree on pilot scope, acceptance criteria, and timeline. Confirm contacts and escalation path.

PILOT SCOPE TEMPLATE (fill during call):
- Objective: (one sentence) e.g., validate chat flow latency < 300ms P50 and relevance > 0.75 on benchmark prompts.
- Primary success metrics: [latency P50/P90, cost per 1k tokens, relevance/accuracy metric, error rate].
- Duration: default 2 weeks (options: 1wk smoke, 4wk extended).
- Traffic profile: baseline rps, burst rps, avg seq len, embedding batch sizes.
- Required infra: cloud region(s), VPC? (yes/no), KMS/HSM required?
- Data handling: sample data types, retention needs, logging level.
- Rollback/fallback tolerance: must have auto-fallback to lower-cost model? (Y/N)
- Roles & contacts: seller (name, email), SE (name), infra lead, security owner.
- Acceptance criteria (explicit pass/fail): e.g., P50 <= 350ms and demo of integration with prefix caching enabled.

SELLER TECHNICAL HANDSHAKE CHECKLIST (quick checkboxes for call):
- [ ] Which API (hosted/dedicated/private)?
- [ ] Expected peak concurrency and sustained throughput
- [ ] Typical request/response token sizes and embedding dims
- [ ] Security: need VPC, IP allowlists, or enterprise KMS?
- [ ] Data residency/regulatory constraints?
- [ ] SLA floor required for pilot? (none, best-effort, or formal)
- [ ] Success metrics agreed and instrumented (tracing/metrics in Redwood Console)

COMMON TECH OBJECTIONS & SELLER SOUND BITES (battlecard snippets):
- Objection: "We need <150ms latency P99 — can you meet it?"
  - Quick soundbite: "We architect for low P50s with batching off for tail requests. For extreme P99s we recommend Dedicated capacity + KV-prefix caching and a model variant pinned for low-latency inference. Let's capture your worst-case RPS and seq length now so we can size the pool."
- Objection: "Costs will balloon with production traffic"
  - Quick soundbite: "We treat cost as a first-class control: adaptive batching, KV caching and quantized model variants can cut unit cost substantially. We'll model your expected token mix during the pilot and show a delta analysis within 48 hours."
- Objection: "I can't send customer data to hosted service."
  - Quick soundbite: "We support Private deployments with VPC and HSM integrations. For pilots we can run in a customer-dedicated project or enable strict retention and redaction controls while we evaluate."

RAPID BATTLECARD TEMPLATES (pick one to attach in email):
- Low-latency chat (quick facts): target P50 < 250ms, recommend Dedicated, small batch, prefix KV cache, model variant: quantized 16-bit low-latency. Key metrics to validate: P50, P90, cold-start penalty.
- Embeddings at scale (quick facts): recommend batching up to 256, async bulk endpoints, use embedding dedupe cache. Key metrics: throughput embeddings/sec, cost per 1k vectors, indexing latency.
- Cost-sensitive rerank (quick facts): use hybrid approach: small in-memory reranker + Redwood-hosted cheap model for candidates. Key metrics: rerank latency, incremental token cost.

ON-PILOT RUNBOOK (day-of checklist for SE and SRE):
- Pre-kickoff (48h): confirm credentials, access to Redwood Console, sample traces push, and baseline benchmark script.
- Day 0: smoke test (send template prompts), enable tracing, set up alert thresholds in Console.
- Day 1–3: monitor latency distribution, check batching ratios and KV cache hit rate, adjust autoscale window if needed.
- Weekly wrap/demo: present dashboard, show cost projection, and capture next-step commitment.

ESCALATION & FALLBACK POLICY (recommended default for pilots):
- If latency > threshold for 2 consecutive hours: automatically enable lower-cost/lower-latency variant and notify SE + infra lead.
- If error rate > 3% or data policy violation: pause traffic, preserve logs, engage security owner.

SELLER EMAIL TEMPLATE (concise):
- Subject: Pilot Kickoff & Quick Tech Checklist
- Body: Hi <Contact>, great to meet. Attached is the one-page pilot scope we agreed on. Please reply with your infra point-of-contact and a snippet of expected traffic (RPS, typical prompt length). We'll provision a sandbox and share access within 48h. — <SE name>

APPENDIX / SAMPLES (short):
- Minimal acceptance example:
  - Metric: P50 <= 300ms, Cost <= $X per 1k tokens, Accuracy >= baseline on sample prompt set
  - Evidence: Console dashboard screenshot + exported trace capturing 200 sample requests

UNRESOLVED / TODO (for this draft):
- Add one-pager for legal (data retention wording for hosted pilots).
- Create a version for retail/embedded integrations that focuses on edge caching.
- Build automated Google Slide export and one-click email generator in SE toolkit.

NOTES TO SELF: short phrases / reminders
- Keep examples concrete (numbers) — sellers skip vague promises.
- Include two micro-decks (1-slide tech, 1-slide economics) per pilot packet.
- Quick toggle: "production-safe?" vs "experiment-only" labeling on pilot docs.

END OF WORKING DRAFT
